data.name: Alleyah
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Alleyah means 'exalted, sublime'. This name is derived from the Arabic root 'l-h-y' which means 'to rise up, to be high'. In Islamic context, it can be associated with Allah's name Al-Mutakabbir, which means 'The Exalted'. The name Alleyah is a beautiful reminder of Allah's greatness and the sublime nature of our faith.

historical_references.reference: Al-Lahi al-Qudus (The Pure One) was a title given to Allah in pre-Islamic Arabian religions. It is believed that this title was used to describe the supreme deity of the Meccan tribe of Quraysh.
historical_references.context: Before the advent of Islam, the Arabs of Mecca worshipped a number of gods, including Al-Lah, whom they believed was the supreme deity. This title, meaning 'The God', was later adopted by the Muslims to refer to Allah as the one and only God.

historical_references.reference: Al-Lah (Allah) was also known as Ar-Rahman (The Most Merciful) and Ar-Rahim (The Most Compassionate) in the Islamic tradition. These titles reflect the belief that Allah is not only the creator of the universe but also the most merciful and compassionate of deities.
historical_references.context: During the early years of Islam, the Prophet Muhammad and his followers developed a theological understanding of Allah as the supreme, merciful, and compassionate deity. These qualities were emphasized in the Quran, and the titles Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim were used to describe Allah's nature.
